correctness.rationale: Every exponent partition of m is realizable using distinct primes, and both divisor counts give the product of f(a)=(a+1)/2. In a maximizer for m>=2, merging 1 with any other part increases the product; splitting a>=6 into 3 and a-3 multiplies the product by 2(a-2)/(a+1)>1. Replacing each 5 by 3+2 preserves the product. Among the remaining parts, 2+2 is worse than 4, 2+4 is worse than 3+3, and 4+4+4 is worse than four 3s. Thus the only candidates by residue are all 3s, one 4 with 3s, or either one 2 or two 4s with 3s. The two-4 pattern wins the last comparison by 25/24 if m>=8. A maximizer with any unreduced 5 would produce a 2 on reduction, hence is possible only at m=5 (a 5 cannot occur at m=2). This recovers every equality case and proves the formulas without a cutoff. Inspected the frozen exact-rational partition verifier and its recorded check through m=40 (215307 partitions); that is supporting evidence only and was not executed.
residual_risks: The theorem is for the denominator 2^omega, not general k; the supplied computational sampling ends at m=40.
